.qc-cache/kittle-2026-10-09-r5/task/solution/app/public/app.js:240-242,297 and public/styles.css:74 (golden highlight is a persistent .focused class)
evidence: Built a criterion -> requirement map for all 28 criteria (2 gates, 16 functional, 6 polish, 4 visual). Every functional criterion traces to a public sentence or the seed data (e.g. exact seven-day boundary -> walls-and-retention.md:67; stale edit keeps typed text -> conversations.md:9; literal %/_ search -> walls-and-retention.md:77; transcript no chat controls -> walls-and-retention.md:79; refusal stays -> walls-and-retention.md:81; live updates keep draft/scroll -> conversations.md:33). Wrong-password refusal, a sign-out control (signin_and_client_scope Part A, polish refusal_in_place) and an emptied composer after Enter are identity/professional defaults covered by the workbook's internal annotation and SKILL known false positive, so not reported. One instance grades an unrequired detail: tests/scored/polish/judge.toml:53 link_highlight demands 'it is still highlighted about ten seconds later', but the only public requirement is conversations.md:17 'takes you to it in its thread and highlights it, so you can spot it at once'. Nothing public requires the highlight to persist; the 10-second persistence mirrors only the golden's permanent .focused class (solution/app/public/app.js:242, styles.css:74). Secondary note (not counted as a defect): sent_once_in_order Part B requires C, A, B order in search results; this is supported by integration/conversations.md:31 'wherever you see them: the thread, search and the transcript', but a newest-first search list (consistently reversed) would be failed - wording is literal enough to stand. No judge run exists for these bytes (raw-evidence-index scope), so the run verdict is from source review only.
counterexample: A conforming app that, on opening a message from a search result or link, scrolls it into view and applies a common 2-3 second yellow flash highlight (Slack/GitHub style fade) satisfies 'highlights it, so you can spot it at once', yet fails polish link_highlight because the highlight is gone at the ten-second check; the polish prompt's every-sentence discipline makes that sentence binding.
suggested_fix: Either remove 'and it is still highlighted about ten seconds later' from link_highlight (check the highlight immediately after opening), or add a public sentence to conversations.md such as 'the highlight stays until you open something else' so the persistence is a stated requirement.
